question: Sunflower plants grow best in soil with a pH range of 6.2 to 6.7. If the pH value of a garden soil is 5, what substance should be added to the soil to grow sunflowers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Compost**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Compost is a natural substance that can help in increasing the pH level of the soil.
 
• It improves soil structure, providing better aeration, drainage, and moisture retention.
 
• Compost adds essential nutrients to the soil, promoting healthy plant growth.
 
• Using compost is an environmentally friendly way to recycle organic waste and enrich the soil.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Soil pH**

 
 
• The pH of soil is a measure of its acidity or alkalinity, ranging from 0 to 14.
 
• A pH below 7 indicates acidic soil, while a pH above 7 indicates alkaline soil.
 
• Most plants, including sunflowers, prefer a slightly acidic to neutral pH range (6.2 to 6.7).
 
 
 
• **Compost**
 
 
• Compost is decomposed organic matter that can be used to improve soil quality.
 
• It contains nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, which are essential for plant growth.
 
• Compost also helps to buffer the soil pH, bringing it closer to the ideal range for plant growth.
 
 
 
• **Soil Amendments**
 
 
• Soil amendments are materials added to soil to improve its physical or chemical properties.
 
• Common soil amendments include compost, lime, sulfur, and organic matter.
 
• The choice of amendment depends on the specific needs of the soil and the plants being grown.
